AND AWARD DATED:5.6.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.7289/2010 ON THE FILE OF THE 24TH ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, 22ND ACMM, MACT,
BANGALORE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UMESH M ADIGA  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the petitioner against the judgment and award dated 05.06.2012, passed by the MACT and XXIV Additional Small Causes Court, Bangalore (for short "the tribunal"), in MVC No.7289/2010, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per the ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case before the Tribunal are as under that on 12.07.2010, at around 11:30 p.m., the petitioner met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing registration No.KA-41-9779 by its driver.
As a result, he sustained grievous injuries.
He took NC: 2025:KHC:25108 HC-KAR treatment as inpatient in CHC Hospital, Kunigal and Dr.K.Narsimaiah Hospital, Tumkur for 8 days.
He spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
He was running a Dhaba and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disability.
With these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.
4. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Both have filed their respective written statement denying the contents of the claim petition.
Respondent No.1 contended that the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and that the policy of insurance was in force as on the date of the accident.
In the event, if claim petition is allowed, the respondent No.2 - Insurer is liable to pay the compensation.
With these reasons, he prayed to dismiss the claim petition against the respondent No1.

Sri B H Raju, S/O Hanumaiah vs Sri Badrappa S/O Channaveerappa on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59671569/
2 5.

The respondent No.2 - Insurer in its written statement denied the contents of the claim petition and denied the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and its NC: 2025:KHC:25108 HC-KAR liability to pay the compensation.
With these reasons, it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues and recorded the evidence.
The petitioner examined two witnesses as PW-1 and PW-2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P27.
The respondents have not led any evidence.

7. The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence on record, awarded following amount of compensation:

1. Pain and sufferings Rs.65,000/-

2. Medical expenses Rs.1,26,000/-

The petitioner being dissatisfied with the award passed by the Tribunal, has filed present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC:25108 HC-KAR 9.
I have heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

10. As per the medical record as well as the evidence of PW-2, the petitioner has suffered following injuries:
i. Fracture right clavicle.
ii. Fracture right 3, 4 ribs.
iii. Blunt Abdomenal Trauma.
Re suturing in Hameio Peritoneal about 2 - 2.5 Liters in the peritoneal cavity.
iv. Haematoma Mesocolon.
v. Middle Colic Artery Tear.
vi. Serosaltear of transverse colon.
vii. Haemo Throax.
11. The evidence of PW-2 was also corroborated by medical records, that is Ex.P6 i.e. X-rays and Scanning films.
The petitioner underwent treatment as an inpatient for 8 days in the said hospital i.e. from 13.07.2010 to 20.07.2010, during which he underwent surgeries.

Considering the evidence of PW- 2, as rightly held by the Tribunal, the petitioner had not suffered from any permanent Sri B H Raju, S/O Hanumaiah vs Sri Badrappa S/O Channaveerappa on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59671569/
3 functional disability, although he might have suffered physical disability.

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month by running a Dhaba.
If that was the case, then he would be an NC: 2025:KHC:25108 HC-KAR income tax assessee as his income would have exceeded Rs.6,00,000/- per annum.
However, he did not produce any documents evidencing the submission of income tax returns to the concerned department.
Hence, the Tribunal has considered the income of petitioner as Rs.3,500/- per month, which is on lower side.
Following the chart of notional income prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.5,500/- per month.
Considering the medical records as well as the evidence of PWs-1 and 2, the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate, which requires enhancement.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for following amount of compensation.
Sl.No Heads Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs.90,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs.1,26,000/-
 3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.16,500/-
 period (5,500/- X 3)
 4. Loss of amenities Rs.75,000/-
 5. Attendant, special diet and Rs.25,000/-
 conveyance charges

Total Rs.3,32,500/-
Less:

Compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.2,41,500/-
 Enhancement Rs.91,000/-
 NC: 2025:KHC:25108  HC-KAR 12.
Undisputedly, respondents are liable to pay the compensation with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
13. Petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.91,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the said amount from the date of petition till its realization.

14. The appeal was filed after delay of 769 days and while allowing the said application, this Court ordered that in the event of enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is not entitled for the interest on the delayed period.

15. For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed.

4 ii)

The impugned the judgment and award dated 05.06.2012, passed in MVC No.
7289/2010 by the MACT and XXIV Additional Small Causes Court, Bangalore, stands modified.
iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhancement of Rs.91,000/- with interest at the rate of NC: 2025:KHC:25108 HC-KAR 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

iv) The petitioner is not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 769 days in filing the appeal.
v) The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall deposit the said amount within a period of six weeks from the date of the award.
vi) Remaining portion of the award of the Tribunal is undisturbed.
vii) Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment.
viii) Draw award accordingly.
